title: Grounding on Request: Learning Modality Control in Vision-Language Models
abstract: arXiv:2610.33841v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: When an image and its caption disagree, can a user reliably control which one a vision-language model (VLM) follows? Accuracy alone cannot answer this question, since a model might give the correct answer from parametric knowledge without following the requested evidence. We therefore evaluate modality grounding control through conflict-preserving counterfactual interventions. Specifically, Flip measures whether an initially correct answer follows an edit to the requested modality, while Stay measures whether it remains stable when the competing modality is edited. To learn this control, we build on neologism learning by introducing new words for visual and textual grounding, training only their embeddings while keeping the pretrained model fixed. translated_title: 按需定位：学习视觉-语言模型中的模态控制
translated_abstract: 当图像与其说明文字相互矛盾时，用户能否可靠地控制视觉-语言模型（VLM）遵循哪一方？仅凭准确率无法回答这个问题，因为模型可能凭借参数化知识给出正确答案，而并未遵循所要求的证据。因此，我们通过保留冲突的反事实干预来评估模态定位控制能力。具体而言，Flip 衡量当被请求的模态被编辑时，最初正确的答案是否会随之改变；Stay 衡量当竞争模态被编辑时，答案是否保持稳定。为了学习这种控制能力，我们在新词学习的基础上，为视觉定位和文本定位引入新词，仅训练它们的嵌入，同时保持预训练模型固定不变。我们还提出了反事实孪生间隔监督，利用成对干预来教导模型：当所请求的证据发生变化时，答案概率应如何相应变化。在……（原文摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 该论文提出通过 Flip/Stay 反事实干预来评估视觉-语言模型的模态定位控制能力，并通过为新词嵌入引入视觉与文本定位标识、结合反事实孪生间隔监督，在冻结预训练模型的前提下教会模型按用户请求遵循指定模态的证据。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces Flip/Stay conflict-preserving counterfactual evaluations and Counterfactual Twin-Margin (CTM) supervision with neologism embeddings to teach frozen vision-language models to reliably follow the modality that the user requests when image and text evidence conflict.
